name: AnimationTrack
simple: An AnimationTrack is the controller for one loaded animation. You get it from Animator:LoadAnimation. With it you can play, stop, speed up, slow down, loop, and listen for when the animation ends or reaches a marked moment.
analogy: An AnimationTrack is like the remote control for one video: Play, Stop, fast-forward (AdjustSpeed), volume (AdjustWeight), and a clock showing how far in you are (TimePosition).
whenToUse: Start and stop an animation (Play, Stop).
Make an animation faster, slower, paused or backward (AdjustSpeed).
Do something at a certain moment in an animation, like a footstep sound (GetMarkerReachedSignal).
Wait for an animation to finish before doing the next thing (Stopped, Ended).
where: You can't create one with Instance.new. Get it from `animator:LoadAnimation(animation)`. Use it in the same kind of script that loaded it: a LocalScript for the player's own character, a server Script for NPCs.

terms.animation: A recorded set of body movements, like a wave or a dance, saved on Roblox with an ID number.
terms.Animation (object): A small object that just holds an animation's ID. It doesn't play anything by itself.
terms.Animator: The object inside a Humanoid (or AnimationController) that actually plays animations on a character.
terms.AnimationTrack: The 'remote control' for one loaded animation. You get it from Animator:LoadAnimation and call Play and Stop on it.
terms.asset ID: The number that identifies something uploaded to Roblox. Animations use it like `rbxassetid://507770239`.
terms.rig: A model set up with joints so it can be animated, like a character.
terms.keyframe: A saved pose at a certain moment in an animation. The animation smoothly moves between keyframes.
terms.fade time: How many seconds an animation takes to smoothly blend in or out, instead of snapping.
terms.weight: How strongly an animation affects the body, from 0 (not at all) to 1 (fully). Used when mixing animations.
terms.priority: Which animation wins when two want to move the same body part. Higher priority (like Action) beats lower (like Idle).
terms.replicate: Copy across the internet so the server and other players see it too.
terms.client: The player's own device. LocalScripts run there.
terms.server: The Roblox computer that runs the game for everyone.
terms.marker: A named point you add to an animation in the Animation Editor, like "Footstep" or "HitFrame". Scripts can listen for it.
terms.animation graph: An advanced animation that mixes several animations based on values (parameters) you set from code.
terms.parameter: A named value you send into an animation graph to control it, like a speed number.

examples.title: Play a wave animation when you press E
examples.code:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

local character = script.Parent
local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
local animator = humanoid:WaitForChild("Animator")

-- 1. Make an Animation object that points to the animation's ID
local waveAnimation = Instance.new("Animation")
waveAnimation.AnimationId = "rbxassetid://507770239" -- Roblox's default R15 wave

-- 2. Load it onto the Animator ONCE to get a track (a remote control)
local waveTrack = animator:LoadAnimation(waveAnimation)
waveTrack.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action -- beat walking/idle animations

-- 3. Play it whenever E is pressed
UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input, typing)
    if typing then
        return -- ignore keys pressed while typing in chat
    end
    if input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.E and not waveTrack.IsPlaying then
        waveTrack:Play()
    end
end)

waveTrack.Stopped:Connect(function()
    print("Done waving")
end)
explain: Three pieces work together: an Animation (holds the ID) -> the Animator (plays it) -> an AnimationTrack (controls it).
Because this script is in StarterCharacterScripts, it is copied into the character each spawn, so script.Parent is the character.
We call LoadAnimation once and reuse the track. Loading again every time would make lots of extra tracks.
Priority Action makes the wave show over the normal walking and idle animations.
Animations a player plays on their own character from a LocalScript are copied to the server and everyone else automatically.
You can only play animations you or your group own (or Roblox's own), otherwise they won't load.

examples.title: Speed, markers, and waiting for the end
examples.code:
local character = script.Parent
local animator = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid"):WaitForChild("Animator")

local animation = Instance.new("Animation")
animation.AnimationId = "rbxassetid://507770239" -- replace with your own animation
local track = animator:LoadAnimation(animation)

-- Runs when the animation reaches a marker named "Clap" (added in the Animation Editor)
track:GetMarkerReachedSignal("Clap"):Connect(function(value)
    print("Clap! Marker value: " .. tostring(value))
end)

track:Play(0.2, 1, 2) -- fade in over 0.2 s, full weight, double speed
print("Length at speed 1: " .. track.Length .. " seconds")

track.Stopped:Wait() -- pause this script until the animation finishes
print("Finished!")
explain: Play takes three optional numbers: fade time (seconds to blend in), weight (0 to 1), and speed (1 is normal, 2 is twice as fast).
Length is how long the animation takes at speed 1. At speed 2 it takes half as long. Length is 0 until the animation has loaded.
GetMarkerReachedSignal fires when the animation passes a named marker. Great for sounds and effects at the exact right moment.
Stopped:Wait() pauses the script until the track stops playing.

gotchas: Load the track once and reuse it. Calling LoadAnimation again makes a new track each time.
Length is 0 until the animation finishes loading. Wait or check that it's above 0.
If two animations move the same body part, the higher Priority wins. Set Priority to Action for attacks and emotes so walking doesn't override them.
Set TimePosition only after calling Play.
After Stop, call Play again before using AdjustWeight.

AnimationTrack.Animation.simple: Read-only. The Animation object this track was loaded from.

AnimationTrack.IsPlaying.simple: Read-only. True while the track is playing. Check it to avoid restarting an animation that's already going.
AnimationTrack.IsPlaying.example:
if not track.IsPlaying then
    track:Play()
end

AnimationTrack.Length.simple: Read-only. How many seconds the animation lasts at normal speed. It's 0 until the animation has loaded.

AnimationTrack.Looped.simple: If true, the animation starts over each time it ends. It starts as whatever was set in the Animation Editor. Changing it while playing takes effect when the current loop ends.

AnimationTrack.Priority.simple: How important this animation is when several play at once. From highest to lowest: Action4, Action3, Action2, Action, Movement, Idle, Core. The higher one controls any body part both try to move.

AnimationTrack.Speed.simple: Read-only. The current playback speed. 1 is normal, 2 is double, 0 is paused, negative plays backward. Change it with AdjustSpeed. Real play time = Length divided by Speed.

AnimationTrack.TimePosition.simple: How many seconds into the animation the track is right now. Set it to jump to a moment (the track must be playing).
AnimationTrack.TimePosition.example:
track:Play()
track.TimePosition = 1.5 -- jump to 1.5 seconds in
track:AdjustSpeed(0)     -- freeze on that pose

AnimationTrack.WeightCurrent.simple: Read-only. How strongly the animation is affecting the body right now (0 to 1). It slides toward WeightTarget over the fade time.

AnimationTrack.WeightTarget.simple: Read-only. The weight the track is fading toward. Set by Play, Stop, and AdjustWeight.
AnimationTrack.WeightTarget.gotcha: Weights are decimal numbers, so compare with a small range (like math.abs(a - b) < 0.001) instead of ==.

AnimationTrack:AdjustSpeed.simple: Changes how fast the animation plays. 1 is normal, 2 is twice as fast, 0.5 is half speed, 0 pauses, and negative numbers play it backward.

AnimationTrack:AdjustWeight.simple: Changes how strongly the animation shows (0 = not at all, 1 = fully), blending over fadeTime seconds. Used to mix animations of the same priority.

AnimationTrack:GetMarkerReachedSignal.simple: Gives an event that fires when the animation reaches a marker with the given name. The marker's value text is passed along. Markers are added in the Animation Editor.

AnimationTrack:GetParameter.simple: For animation graphs: reads back a parameter value you set with SetParameter. Gives nil if it was never set.

AnimationTrack:GetParameterDefaults.simple: For animation graphs: gives a table of all parameters the graph has and their starting values. Empty if it's a normal animation.
AnimationTrack:GetParameterDefaults.example:
for name, value in track:GetParameterDefaults() do
    print(name, value)
end

AnimationTrack:GetTimeOfKeyframe.simple: Gives the time (in seconds) of the first keyframe with a certain name. Errors if the name doesn't exist or the animation hasn't loaded (Length is still 0).

AnimationTrack:Play.simple: Starts the animation. Optional: fadeTime (seconds to blend in, default 0.1), weight (default 1), speed (default 1).
AnimationTrack:Play.example:
track:Play() -- normal
track:Play(0.5, 1, 1.5) -- blend in over half a second, 1.5x speed

AnimationTrack:SetParameter.simple: For animation graphs: sets a named parameter that controls the graph. Can be set before or during playback.

AnimationTrack:Stop.simple: Stops the animation, fading it out over fadeTime seconds (default 0.1).
AnimationTrack:Stop.example: track:Stop(0.5) -- fade out over half a second

AnimationTrack.DidLoop.simple: Fires each time a looped animation finishes one loop and starts again.
AnimationTrack.DidLoop.example:
local loops = 0
track.DidLoop:Connect(function()
    loops += 1
    print("Loop #" .. loops)
end)

AnimationTrack.Ended.simple: Fires when the track is completely done: finished playing, finished fading out, and the body is back to normal. Good for cleanup.

AnimationTrack.Stopped.simple: Fires as soon as the track stops playing (it may still be fading out). Great for playing animations one after another.
